beginner.summary: For developers who know another language such as Java, Python, C# or JavaScript and are new to Scala 3. Covers installing the JDK, Coursier and Scala CLI, vals and types, expression-based control flow, methods and functions, strings, immutable collections and their transformations, classes, traits, case classes and enums, pattern matching, Option, Either and Try, for comprehensions, generics and variance, givens and extension methods, packages, file handling, munit testing, sbt builds and a command-line tool capstone.
prerequisites: Writes working programs in at least one other language such as Java, Python, C# or JavaScript
Uses a terminal confidently: changing directories, running commands and setting environment variables
Has a laptop with rights to install a JDK, Coursier and an editor such as Visual Studio Code with Metals or IntelliJ IDEA
outcomes: Install the Scala 3 toolchain and build, run and test programs with Scala CLI and sbt
Model data with case classes, enums and traits and process it with immutable collections and pattern matching
Handle absence and failure with Option, Either and Try instead of null and exceptions
Build, test and package a command-line tool that reads files and reports errors with correct exit codes

intermediate.summary: For Scala developers who can write idiomatic Scala 3 and now build services. Covers type classes and derivation, opaque, union and intersection types, context functions, migration from Scala 2.13, lazy evaluation, stack safety, typed errors, Future, Cats, Cats Effect, fs2, circe, http4s and Tapir, doobie and Flyway, ScalaCheck, direct-style concurrency with Ox, ZIO 2, running Spark from Scala 3, and a service capstone.
prerequisites: Completes the beginner level or has equivalent experience with Scala 3 collections, case classes, pattern matching and sbt
Understands HTTP, JSON and relational databases at the level of writing a simple CRUD application
Has Docker installed for running PostgreSQL and other test containers
outcomes: Design type-safe domain models and type classes using givens, opaque types and derivation
Write concurrent and streaming programs with Cats Effect, fs2, Ox or ZIO
Build and test an HTTP and database service with http4s, Tapir, circe and doobie
Migrate and build Scala code across Scala 2.13 and Scala 3 and use 2.13 libraries such as Spark safely

advanced.summary: For experienced Scala engineers who build libraries and production systems. Covers match types, inline and quoted macros, Mirror-based derivation, dependent and polymorphic function types, explicit nulls and capture checking, tagless final, JVM memory and GC profiling, JMH, Apache Pekko actors, streams and event sourcing, Scala.js, Scala Native and GraalVM, compiler internals and plugins, binary compatibility with MiMa, observability, dependency security, production troubleshooting and a hardened-service capstone.
prerequisites: Completes the intermediate level or has equivalent production experience with Scala 3, an effect library and sbt
Reads JVM concepts such as heap, garbage collection and thread pools without help
Can run Docker, a CI system and a profiler on a development machine
outcomes: Use inline, match types, macros and Mirrors to remove boilerplate while keeping compile errors clear
Profile, benchmark and troubleshoot Scala services on the JVM with JFR, JMH, async-profiler and heap dumps
Build distributed, event-sourced systems with Apache Pekko and instrument them with OpenTelemetry
Publish binary-compatible libraries and target JavaScript and native platforms from one code base
